label: hv-mat-biomaterials
topic: Biomaterial mixing, foam, water-uptake and bilayer laws for bio-based printable materials: harvest, formal statements, registry overlap, falsifying tests, two validations, one Lean file
summary:
Ten statements harvested and formalised; three checks run against one open paper (Islam et al. 2017, fungal mycelium, full text opened via Europe PMC); one Lean file passes check.sh with ALL CHECKED on the first run.

Validation results (all from Islam 2017, densities 30-50 kg/m3):
- Stiffness exponent: PASS, loosely. Gibson-Ashby predicts 2; the paper's reported end-point ranges (600-2000 kPa) imply about 2.36. This is my arithmetic on rounded ranges, not a refit of their data; the authors themselves report square scaling.
- Absolute stiffness with prefactor C = 1: FAIL. Using the paper's chitin wall values (2.5 GPa, 1430 kg/m3) the law predicts 1100 and 3056 kPa at 30 and 50 kg/m3; measured is about 600 and 2000 kPa (ratio 0.55-0.65). Using the hyphal wall modulus the paper also quotes (110-140 MPa) it predicts 48-62 kPa at 30 kg/m3, roughly 10 times too low. The scaling holds; the prefactor and the choice of solid modulus do not transfer.
- Yield strength, exponent 1.5: PASS. Predicted 41 and 88 kPa; measured 40-80 kPa. The 0.3 prefactor is the Gibson-Ashby textbook value from memory, not from a source I opened.

Lean: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-mat-biomaterials/HalpinTsaiBounds.lean proves five theorems with standard axioms only. The new content is that the Halpin-Tsai closed form lies between the Reuss and Voigt bounds for any shape factor xi >= 0, and equals Reuss at xi = 0. This is algebra on the closed forms, not a derivation from elasticity. The fifth theorem (doubling density quadruples stiffness) is a trivial identity.

Registry overlap: Voigt-Reuss ordering and equality case already exist (tracks/research/lean/bm-lean-materials-laws__VoigtReuss.lean); the Timoshenko bilayer ceiling already exists (tracks/lean/HygromorphCeiling.lean). Halpin-Tsai has no hit anywhere in lean, tracks/lean or tracks/research. Fickian uptake and Gibson-Ashby are mentioned in tracks/research but I found no Lean theorem for them (file-name grep only; I did not read those files).

Limits: of the primary sources, only Islam 2017 was opened in full text. Voigt 1889, Reuss 1929, Timoshenko 1925, Gibson-Ashby 1982 and Hashin-Shtrikman 1963 were confirmed as Crossref records only; the Halpin-Kardos DOI was confirmed from the Wikipedia reference list; the Hill 1952 and Shen-Springer 1976 Crossref lookups failed. The quantitative forms for those are the standard textbook ones, written from memory. No fibre-composite or water-uptake dataset was fetched, so statements 1-4, 6 and 8-10 are untested here. The "open dataset" named for each of those is a class of data, not a located file.

findings.claim: S1 Voigt upper bound (rule of mixtures, equal strain). Formal: for a two-phase composite with phase moduli E1,E2 > 0 and volume fraction 0 <= f <= 1, E_eff <= f E1 + (1-f) E2. Assumptions: linear elastic, perfectly bonded phases, no porosity. Registry: ALREADY PRESENT as closed-form ordering (reuss_le_voigt in tracks/research/lean/bm-lean-materials-laws__VoigtReuss.lean). Falsifying test: any open table of flax/PLA or wood-flour/PLA printed-filament tensile moduli with fibre volume fraction; fail if a measured modulus exceeds f Ef + (1-f) Em beyond measurement error.
findings.evidence_quote: E_V = fE1 + (1-f)E2 (as extracted from the page)
findings.confidence: high for the form; primary paper not opened; no dataset located or tested

findings.claim: S2 Reuss lower bound (equal stress). Formal: 1/E_R = f/E1 + (1-f)/E2 and E_eff >= E_R. Same assumptions as S1; porosity breaks it. Registry: ALREADY PRESENT (same VoigtReuss.lean, including the equality case reuss_eq_voigt_iff). Falsifying test: same composite tables; a measured modulus below E_R falsifies the no-porosity, perfect-bond assumptions rather than the algebra.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_mixtures (opened; formula text garbled in extraction); primary Reuss 1929 doi:10.1002/zamm.19290090104 (Crossref record only)
findings.confidence: high for the form; primary not opened; not tested

findings.claim: S3 Halpin-Tsai. Formal: E/Em = (1 + xi eta phi)/(1 - eta phi), eta = (Ef/Em - 1)/(Ef/Em + xi), xi >= 0 a shape factor (commonly 2 L/d for longitudinal modulus of short fibres). Assumptions: aligned fibres, perfect bond, xi fitted or set by geometry. Registry: ABSENT (no grep hit for Halpin in lean, tracks/lean or tracks/research). Falsifying test: short-fibre biocomposite modulus versus fibre aspect ratio at fixed phi; fail if the xi needed to fit the data is negative, i.e. the measured modulus falls outside the Reuss-Voigt interval.
findings.source: Halpin and Kardos 1976, doi:10.1002/pen.760160512 (not opened; citation confirmed on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halpin-Tsai_model, which gives no equations)
findings.confidence: medium: equation written from memory, the opened page describes the model in words only; the xi = 2L/d convention is also from memory

findings.claim: S4 (new, Lean-checked) Halpin-Tsai is bracketed by the mixture bounds: for Em, Ef > 0, 0 <= phi <= 1, xi >= 0, Reuss <= HT(xi) <= Voigt, and HT(0) = Reuss exactly. Uses the closed form HT = Em (Ef + xi V)/(D + xi Em), V = phi Ef + (1-phi) Em, D = (1-phi) Ef + phi Em. Registry: ABSENT before this file. Falsifying test: none for the algebra; it means a Halpin-Tsai fit can never explain a measurement outside the bounds.
findings.evidence_quote: ALL CHECKED: no errors, no sorryAx
findings.confidence: high for the algebra; the equivalence of the closed form to the eta form was done by hand in a comment, not proved in Lean

findings.claim: S5 Gibson-Ashby open-cell stiffness scaling. Formal: E/Es = C (rho/rho_s)^2 with C about 1, for bending-dominated open cells at low relative density. Registry: mentioned in tracks/research (bm-lean-materials-laws, bm-mycelium-living-materials); no Lean theorem found. Falsifying test: log-log regression of modulus on density for mycelium foams; fail if the slope's confidence interval excludes 2.
findings.source: Islam et al. 2017, Sci Rep, doi:10.1038/s41598-017-13295-2 (full text opened via Europe PMC PMC5638950); primary Gibson and Ashby 1982 doi:10.1098/rspa.1982.0088 (Crossref record only)
findings.evidence_quote: For open cell foams, the exponents are 2 for the elastic modulus
findings.confidence: high for the form as quoted by Islam; C about 1 is from memory; primary not opened

findings.claim: VALIDATION A (exponent): PASS, loosely. Prediction: slope 2. Measured: modulus 600 to 2000 kPa over 30 to 50 kg/m3 gives ln(3.33)/ln(1.667) = 2.36. Authors state square scaling from their own fit.
findings.value: predicted 2; implied from reported ranges about 2.36
findings.evidence_quote: the modulus varies with the square of mycelium density
findings.confidence: medium: my figure uses rounded end-point ranges, assuming the low modulus pairs with the low density; not a refit of the raw points

findings.claim: VALIDATION B (absolute stiffness, C = 1): FAIL. With chitin wall Es = 2.5 GPa and rho_s = 1430 kg/m3 the law predicts 1100 kPa at 30 kg/m3 and 3056 kPa at 50 kg/m3; measured about 600 and 2000 kPa (ratio 0.55 to 0.65). With the hyphal wall modulus 110-140 MPa also quoted in the paper it predicts 48-62 kPa at 30 kg/m3, about 10 times below measurement.
findings.evidence_quote: varies from 600 to 2000 kPa for the given range of density
findings.confidence: medium: solid-phase values are the paper's literature values for chitin, not measured on these samples; a fibre network is not a true cellular foam

findings.claim: S6 / VALIDATION C Gibson-Ashby open-cell strength. Formal: sigma_y = C2 sigma_ys (rho/rho_s)^(3/2), C2 about 0.3. Prediction with sigma_ys = 45 MPa, rho_s = 1430 kg/m3: 41 kPa at 30 kg/m3, 88 kPa at 50 kg/m3. Measured yield 40-80 kPa. PASS. Registry: no Lean theorem found. Falsifying test: same mycelium density series; fail if the strength slope's interval excludes 1.5.
findings.value: predicted 41 to 88 kPa; measured 40 to 80 kPa
findings.confidence: medium: exponent and measured range are quoted; the 0.3 prefactor is from memory, not from an opened source

findings.claim: S7 Timoshenko bilayer curvature. Formal: kappa = 6 (1+m)^2 d_eps / ( h [ 3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn)) ] ), m = thickness ratio, n = modulus ratio, h = total thickness, d_eps = differential (hygro)expansion strain; maximum 3 d_eps/(2h) when m^2 n = 1. Assumptions: Euler-Bernoulli beam, uniform strain per layer, perfect bond. Registry: ALREADY PRESENT (tracks/lean/HygromorphCeiling.lean: timoshenkoCoefficient_le, bilayerCurvature_optimal, bilayer_rules_out). Falsifying test: printed wood-fibre/PLA hygromorph curvature tables; fail if measured curvature exceeds 3 d_eps/(2h).
findings.confidence: medium: formula from memory, consistent with theorem names in the repo; primary not opened; not tested here

findings.claim: S8 Fickian water uptake, short time. Formal: for a plate of thickness h exposed on both faces, M_t/M_inf = (4/h) sqrt(D t/pi) while M_t/M_inf < about 0.6. Assumptions: constant D, no swelling, one-dimensional diffusion. Registry: Fickian is mentioned in tracks/research (bm-bilayer-theory-verified, bm-building-physics-standards); no Lean theorem found. Falsifying test: mass gain versus sqrt(t) for immersed natural-fibre/PLA coupons; fail if the early curve is not linear in sqrt(t) or D differs across thicknesses.
findings.source: Shen and Springer 1976, J Compos Mater, doi:10.1177/002199767601000101 (Crossref lookup failed; not opened)
findings.confidence: low on the citation (DOI unverified); the formula is the standard one from memory; not tested

findings.claim: S9 Fickian thickness scaling. Formal: time to reach a fixed fractional uptake scales as h^2 (t_half is about 0.049 h^2/D for a plate). Registry: no Lean theorem found. Falsifying test: uptake curves for printed coupons at two thicknesses; fail if the half-time ratio differs from the thickness ratio squared. Natural-fibre composites often swell, so failure is plausible.
findings.source: Standard result of the plate diffusion solution; no source opened
findings.confidence: low: from memory, no source opened, not tested

findings.claim: S10 Hashin-Shtrikman bounds are tighter than Voigt-Reuss for isotropic two-phase composites. Formal (bulk modulus, K2 > K1, G1 the softer shear modulus): K_lower = K1 + f2 / ( 1/(K2-K1) + 3 f1/(3K1 + 4G1) ), with Reuss <= HS_lower <= HS_upper <= Voigt. Assumptions: statistically isotropic, well-ordered phases. Registry: ABSENT (not in VoigtReuss.lean theorem list). Falsifying test: isotropic particulate biocomposite (e.g. wood-flour filled) moduli; fail if a measurement lies outside the HS interval.
findings.source: Hashin and Shtrikman 1963, doi:10.1016/0022-5096(63)90060-7 (Crossref record only)
findings.confidence: medium: formula from memory; primary not opened; not tested

lay_summary: Engineers have simple rules for guessing how stiff a material made of two ingredients will be, how stiff a sponge-like material is, how fast it soaks up water, and how much a two-layer strip curls.
We wrote ten of these rules down precisely and checked which ones the project already has.
We tested the sponge rule on a real mushroom-root material: the rule gets the trend right (denser means much stiffer) but guesses the actual stiffness almost twice too high.
The matching rule for strength landed almost exactly on the measured numbers.
We also got a computer proof checker to confirm that one popular fibre formula can never give an answer outside the two simplest limits.

glossary.Young's modulus (E): How stiff a material is: the force per area needed to stretch it by a given fraction.
glossary.Rule of mixtures: Estimating a blend's property as a weighted average of its ingredients.
glossary.Voigt bound: The highest stiffness a two-ingredient material can have, as if both ingredients stretch equally side by side.
glossary.Reuss bound: The lowest stiffness, as if the ingredients are stacked in series and carry the same load.
glossary.Volume fraction (f, phi): The share of the material's volume taken up by one ingredient.
glossary.Halpin-Tsai: A formula for the stiffness of a plastic filled with short fibres, with a knob for fibre shape.
glossary.Shape factor (xi): The knob in Halpin-Tsai; bigger for longer, thinner fibres.
glossary.Hashin-Shtrikman bounds: Tighter upper and lower stiffness limits for a blend that looks the same in every direction.
glossary.Gibson-Ashby scaling: A rule saying a foam's stiffness goes as its density squared, and its strength as density to the power 1.5.
glossary.Open-cell foam: A sponge-like solid whose pores connect to each other.
glossary.Relative density: Foam density divided by the density of the solid it is made of.
glossary.Prefactor (C): The constant multiplier in front of a scaling rule.
glossary.Yield strength: The stress at which a material stops springing back and deforms permanently.
glossary.Mycelium: The thread-like root network of a fungus.
glossary.Chitin: The stiff natural polymer in fungal cell walls.
glossary.Fickian diffusion: Spreading of a substance (here water) driven only by concentration differences, at a constant rate coefficient.
glossary.Timoshenko bilayer: A formula for how much a two-layer strip curls when one layer expands more than the other.
glossary.Curvature (kappa): How sharply something bends; one over the bend radius.
glossary.Hygromorph: A part that changes shape when it takes up moisture.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer proof checker and its maths library.
glossary.Axiom: A starting assumption a proof is allowed to rest on.
glossary.sorry: A Lean placeholder meaning 'not actually proved'.
glossary.Crossref: A public index of published papers and their DOIs.
glossary.DOI: A permanent identifier for a published paper.
glossary.kPa, MPa, GPa: Units of stress or stiffness: thousand, million and billion pascals.

recommendations: Add Halpin-Tsai bracketing to the law registry from HalpinTsaiBounds.lean, and add a Lean proof that the closed form equals the eta form (currently only a hand derivation in a comment).

Find one open flax/PLA or wood/PLA table (fibre fraction, modulus) and one water-uptake time series so statements S1-S4 and S8-S9 get a real test.
